mainTopic: Three lessons from a half-consecrated animal, אביי's question about one animal with two holy labels, and the new משנה on which words create a תמורה, including the double meaning of תחת.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of רבי יוחנן's ruling: when someone makes only half an animal holy, the animal is holy but cannot be offered, and its תמורה is treated the same way. From this the גמרא learns three rules. קדושת דמים can push an animal off the מזבח for good, living animals can be pushed off, and being pushed off from the very start still counts as דיחוי. Next, אביי says everyone agrees that an animal labeled 'half עולה, half מעשר' is offered entirely as an עולה. He then asks about 'half תמורה, half מעשר': is it offered as a תמורה, since תמורה applies to all קדשים, or as מעשר, since מעשר can make holy the animals before and after the tenth? The question ends with תיקו, unresolved. A new משנה follows. Words like 'in place of', 'substitute of' and 'exchange for' create a תמורה, but 'desacralized onto' does not, unless the holy animal is blemished, in which case it is redeemed and the values must be evened out. The גמרא asks why the משנה treats תחת as substitution wording, when a ברייתא about בדק הבית property treats it as redemption wording. אביי answers that תחת can mean either one, and he begins bringing a פסוק for the substitution meaning, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The substitute of a half-consecrated animal is the same
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of רבי יוחנן's ruling: the תמורה of a half-consecrated animal shares its status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's ruling from just before this point. A half-consecrated animal is holy but cannot be offered, and its תמורה (substitute) is treated the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main animal is holy, but since only half of it was consecrated, it can never go on the מזבח. Its תמורה follows the animal it replaced, so it too is holy but never offered. This ruling is the base for the three lessons in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Like it, the same as it
A substitute animal that becomes holy when someone tries to swap it for a holy animal

phrases.english: is like it.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי יוחנן's statement from just before: the תמורה of the half-consecrated animal is holy but not offered, just like the original.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's ruling that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal consecrated only halfway is holy but not offered, and its תמורה has the same status.

steps.title: Three lessons learned from רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוחנן's ruling the גמרא learns three rules about דיחוי (being permanently pushed off the מזבח).
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. First, holiness of value (קדושת דמים) causes the animal to be pushed off. Second, living animals can be pushed off. Third, being pushed off from the very start counts as being pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls three general rules out of רבי יוחנן's ruling about a half-consecrated animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrating half an animal only gives it קדושת דמים, yet it still ends up permanently unfit for the מזבח. That teaches lesson 1: קדושת דמים can cause דיחוי. The animal is alive, which teaches lesson 2: דיחוי works on living animals, not just on slaughtered ones. It was never fit even for a moment, which teaches lesson 3: דיחוי מעיקרו, being pushed off from the start, is still a real דיחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, conclude from this
Holiness of value only, not holiness of the body of the animal itself
Being permanently pushed off from being offered on the מזבח
Living animals
From the very beginning

steps.whatToRemember: A half-consecrated animal teaches three rules. קדושת דמים can cause דיחוי, living animals can be נדחין, and דיחוי מעיקרו counts as דיחוי.
steps.confusionAlert: דיחוי מעיקרו does not mean the animal was fit and then became unfit. It means it was never fit from the moment it was consecrated, and it is still considered pushed off.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three rules about דיחוי are used in many other places in קדשים, so they are well worth remembering.

phrases.english: Learn three things from this:
Learn from it that holiness of value causes [the animal] to be pushed off.
phrases.notes: Some versions say נדחה, 'is pushed off'; the words in square brackets give the corrected wording, מדחה, 'pushes off'. Either way, the animal ends up permanently unfit.

phrases.english: And learn from it that living animals can be pushed off,
phrases.notes: Some versions say מומין, 'blemished animals'; the words in square brackets give the corrected wording, חיים, 'living animals'.

phrases.english: And learn from it that being pushed off from the start
counts as being pushed off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws general rules out of the ruling that was just completed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קדושת דמים causes דיחוי, living animals can be pushed off, and דיחוי מעיקרו is a real דיחוי.

steps.title: Half burnt offering, half tithe: it is offered as a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: אביי says everyone agrees that an animal labeled 'half עולה, half מעשר' is offered entirely as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees that where someone said 'half of it is an עולה and half of it is מעשר', all agree the animal is offered as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new discussion about one animal given two different holy labels. He starts with a case where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'this is מעשר' does nothing, because מעשר בהמה only becomes holy through the counting process. So only the עולה label takes hold. The whole animal goes to the מזבח as an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
A burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח
Here, מעשר בהמה: the tenth animal, made holy through counting
Is offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: Abaye said: Everyone agrees
where one said: 'Half of it is a burnt offering
and half of it is a tithe' —
all agree it is offered as a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: one animal with two holy labels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Half עולה, half מעשר' means the whole animal is offered as an עולה.

steps.title: Half substitute, half tithe: what is the law?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks about an animal labeled 'half תמורה, half מעשר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where someone said 'half of it is a תמורה and half of it is מעשר', what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי moves to a harder case and asks a question. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the עולה case, the עולה label clearly wins. Here, neither label works in the normal way: a תמורה needs a holy animal to swap with, and מעשר needs the counting process. The question is which of the two kinds of holiness decides how the animal is offered. The next step lays out both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What is the law?

phrases.english: Where one said: 'Half of it is a substitute
and half of it is a tithe' — what [is the law]?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר ״חֶצְיָהּ תְּמוּרָה וְחֶצְיָהּ מַעֲשֵׂר״, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the agreed case of step 3 by swapping עולה for תמורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When an animal is labeled half תמורה and half מעשר, is it offered as a תמורה or as מעשר?

steps.title: The two sides of אביי's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the 'half תמורה, half מעשר' case is a real doubt: each kind of holiness has a reason to be the stronger one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the animal offered as a תמורה, because תמורה applies to every kind of holy animal? Or is it offered as מעשר, because מעשר is so strong that it can make holy even the animals counted before and after the tenth by mistake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out the two possible answers to the question אביי asked in the previous step. Each side gets its own reason for why it should 'win'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: תמורה is stronger because it is wide-reaching, since it works on all קדשים. Side two: מעשר is stronger because it is so powerful that it can even make holy the 9th or 11th animal if the owner mistakenly called it 'tenth'. The question is which kind of strength decides how the animal is offered.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal that passes under the rod becomes holy.
Makes holy the animals before and after it: the 9th or 11th, if mistakenly called 'tenth'.

phrases.english: Is it offered as a substitute,
since it applies to all consecrated animals,
or perhaps it is offered as a tithe animal,
since it consecrates the animals before it and after it?
phrases.notes: If the owner miscounts and calls the 9th or 11th animal 'tenth', that animal becomes holy too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question אביי asked in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which holiness decides how the animal is offered: the wide-reaching holiness of תמורה, or the powerful holiness of מעשר?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot decide between the two sides, so the question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question is not answered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends אביי's question with תיקו, meaning no answer was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons from the last step are strong, and no source settles which one wins. So the case of an animal that is half תמורה and half מעשר stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it stand': the question remains unanswered.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's 'half תמורה, half מעשר' question ends without an answer (תיקו). Is תמורה stronger because it applies to all קדשים, or is מעשר stronger because it can make holy the animals before and after the tenth?

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question laid out in step 5 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question is unresolved: there is no ruling on whether such an animal is offered as a תמורה or as מעשר.

steps.title: Which words create a substitute
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists the phrases that make a non-sacred animal into a תמורה, and one phrase that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'This is in place of that,' 'This is the substitute of that,' or 'This is the exchange for that,' the animal becomes a תמורה. If he says 'This one is desacralized onto that one,' it is not a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches which wording turns a regular animal into a substitute for a holy animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words of swapping (תחת, תמורה, חליפה) create a תמורה, so both animals end up holy. The phrase 'מחוללת על' is the language of redemption, which means moving the holiness off one animal. That is a different act, so it does not make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: our משנה.
'In place of'.
'The exchange for'.
'Desacralized onto': language of redeeming, which moves holiness off an item.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תמורה with חילול. In a תמורה the original animal stays holy and the new one becomes holy too. In a חילול the holiness moves off the original, and that only works in certain cases.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"This is hereby in place of that,"
"the substitute of that," "the exchange for that"
that animal is a substitute.
"This one is desacralized onto that one"
phrases.notes: Here 'this one' is the holy animal, and he is trying to move its holiness onto the regular animal.

phrases.english: that is not a substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic: the wording of תמורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Words of swapping (תחת, תמורת, חליפת) create a תמורה; words of redemption (מחוללת על) do not.

steps.title: When the holy animal is blemished
steps.stepSummary: If the holy animal has a blemish, saying 'desacralized onto' really does redeem it, but the values must be evened out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the holy animal was blemished, it becomes non-sacred, and he must work out the values.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the 'מחוללת' wording. It teaches that this wording does work when the holy animal has a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished holy animal can be redeemed, so 'this is desacralized onto that' actually takes its holiness away. Still, the owner must compare the two animals' values. If the holy animal was worth more, the הקדש must not lose out.

keyTerms.meaning: Blemished: an animal with a defect that makes it unfit for the מזבח.
Goes out to non-sacred status: it loses its holiness.
To make up the value: compare prices and pay any difference to הקדש.

phrases.english: And if the consecrated animal was blemished,
it goes out to non-sacred status,
and he is required to make up the value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a special case to the 'מחוללת' wording from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a blemished holy animal, 'desacralized onto' redeems it, but the owner must even out the values.

steps.title: Does תחת really mean substitution?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the משנה's assumption that תחת is a word of substitution, and starts bringing a ברייתא about Temple-maintenance property that seems to contradict it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that 'in place of' is language of transferring holiness? But compare a ברייתא: with קדשי בדק הבית, if he said 'the exchange for that' or 'the substitute of that,' he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to the משנה's first phrase, תחת. It quotes a ברייתא about property given for Temple upkeep, setting up a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה put תחת in the same list as תמורה and חליפה, which suggests it is substitution language. The ברייתא starts by saying that for בדק הבית, the words 'exchange' and 'substitute' do nothing, since תמורה does not apply there. The contradiction about תחת itself will become clear as the ברייתא continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא: the discussion of the משנה.
'Is that to say…': opens a question about what follows from a statement.
Language of 'catching' or transferring holiness, meaning substitution wording.
'And they contrasted it': introduces a source that seems to contradict.
Items given for Temple maintenance, not for the מזבח.
'He said nothing': the statement has no effect.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is that to say that "in place of"
is a term of transferring holiness?
And they raised a contradiction:
With items consecrated for Temple maintenance,
if he said "the exchange for that" or "the substitute of that,"
he has said nothing.
phrases.notes: These are substitution words, and תמורה does not work on Temple-maintenance property, so nothing happens.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּתַחַת לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַתְפּוֹסֵי הוּא, וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's listing of תחת as substitution language in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implication that תחת is a term of substitution.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about קדשי בדק הבית, which begins by treating 'exchange' and 'substitute' as ineffective there, is brought to show that תחת may be treated differently from real substitution words.

steps.title: The ending of the ברייתא makes תחת look like a word of redemption
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: saying 'in place of this' or 'desacralized onto this' does take effect on בדק הבית property. The גמרא asks why תחת would act differently from the substitution words in the first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'in place of this' or 'desacralized onto this', his words stand. Now, if you think תחת is a word of substitution, why should the first clause be different from the last clause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in step 9 and then states the contradiction clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause of the ברייתא says substitution words like 'exchange' and 'substitute' do nothing for בדק הבית property. The last clause says תחת does work, just like 'desacralized'. So the ברייתא seems to treat תחת as a redemption word, not a substitution word. That clashes with our משנה, which lists תחת as a word that makes a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: His words stand: what he said takes effect
The first clause of a ברייתא or משנה
The last clause of a ברייתא or משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Substitution (תמורה) and redemption (חילול) are different things. With substitution, both animals end up holy. With redemption, the holiness moves over and the original item becomes non-holy.

phrases.english: [But if he said:] 'In place of this,' or 'desacralized onto this'
his words stand.
And if it enters your mind
that [תחת] is a word of substitution,
what is different about the first clause
and what is different about the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאִיתְּפוֹסֵי הִיא, מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 9 and spells out how it contradicts the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption (step 7) that תחת is a word of substitution.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets תחת redeem בדק הבית property, but it says substitution words cannot. So תחת must not be a substitution word.

steps.title: אביי: the word תחת can mean two things
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that תחת is used both as a word of substitution and as a word of redemption. He begins bringing a פסוק for the substitution meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: you find 'in place of' used as a word of substitution, and also as a word of redemption. As a word of substitution, as it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by saying the word תחת has two meanings. He starts bringing a פסוק to prove the first one, and the פסוק itself comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is really no contradiction. The משנה uses תחת in its substitution sense, for קרבנות. The ברייתא uses it in its redemption sense, for בדק הבית property. Since the Torah uses the word both ways, each source can read it the way that fits its case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In place of': the word whose meaning is under discussion
You find it: this word shows up in more than one way
A word of redemption: it moves the holiness off the item

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's key idea is that one word, תחת, can carry two meanings. It means substitution in one setting and redemption in another.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
'In place of': you find it as
a word of substitution
and a word of redemption.
A word of substitution, as it is written:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: ״תַּחַת״ מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאִיתְּפוֹסֵי וְלִישָּׁנָא דְּאַחוֹלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the word has two meanings, one for each source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תחת has only one meaning, so the משנה and the ברייתא clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: תחת can mean substitution or redemption. The משנה uses one meaning and the ברייתא uses the other.
